Dukstas Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Utenos apskritis, Lithuania

Not demolished. Dūkštas began developing after railway construction in 1863, drawing Jewish settlers even before formal settlement was officially permitted there in 1903; by 1867, about 600 Jews already made up two-thirds of the town. The community built a synagogue and beit-midrash, and opened a modern cheder alongside the traditional one before WWI. Many residents left during WWI but most returned; by 1925, the Jewish population reached 643 (69 percent), supported by both Hebrew and Yiddish schools and a People's Bank helping small businesses survive economic crises. Following the German invasion of 1941, Jews were confined to two ghetto areas and forced into labor; on September 22, 1941, all remaining Jews were murdered in a nearby forest.
